theme: The centurion; the widow’s son; the sinful woman; the Sower
readingInstruction: Read Luke 7:1-8:21. A Gentile’s faith, a widow’s son, a sinful woman, and the parable of the sower. Notice who Jesus honors, and who he rebukes.
settingTheScene: After the Sermon on the Plain, Jesus enters Capernaum and then Nain, then dines with a Pharisee, then tells parables by the lake. Luke gathers stories that show Jesus’ compassion for the outsider: a Roman soldier, a widow, a woman with a bad reputation. These are the people the religious leaders overlooked. Jesus will respond to John the Baptist’s doubts by pointing to what he is doing.
observation: “I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such faith” (7:9).
“And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her and said to her, Do not weep” (7:13).
“The blind receive their sight, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, the poor have good news preached to them” (7:22).
“But he who is forgiven little, loves little” (7:47).
“Your faith has saved you; go in peace” (7:50).
“The seed is the word of God” (8:11).
“And as for that in the good soil, they are those who, hearing the word, hold it fast in an honest and good heart, and bear fruit with patience” (8:15).
“My mother and my brothers are those who hear the word of God and do it” (8:21).
interpretation:
A Roman centurion sends friends to ask Jesus to heal his servant. He says he is not worthy to have Jesus come under his roof, and that Jesus need only say the word. Jesus marvels, and says he has not found such faith in Israel. A pagan soldier understood authority better than the religious insiders. Faith is believing that Jesus’ word is enough.

At Nain, Jesus meets a funeral procession. A widow’s only son is dead. Luke notes simply that when the Lord saw her, he had compassion. He touches the bier, speaks, and the young man sits up. Jesus gives him back to his mother. The crowd says, “God has visited his people!” That is the right conclusion.

John the Baptist, now in prison, sends disciples to ask whether Jesus is the one. Jesus does not give a direct yes. He tells them to report what they see and hear: the blind see, the lame walk, the dead are raised, the poor hear good news. These are the signs of Isaiah’s promised age.

In Simon the Pharisee’s house, an uninvited woman, known as a sinner, weeps on Jesus’ feet, wipes them with her hair, and anoints them. Simon is scandalized. Jesus tells a story of two debtors, one forgiven a large debt and one a small debt. The one forgiven more loves more. Then he turns to the woman and says, “Your sins are forgiven.” Her love was the result of forgiveness, not the cause. Simon, who thought he needed little, loved little.

The parable of the sower closes the section. The seed is the word, and the soils are hearts. Some hearts are hard, some shallow, some choked, and some good. The good soil hears, holds fast, and bears fruit with patience. Jesus’ real family are not those with the right blood but those who hear and do the word of God.
connection: Isaiah 35:5-6 and 61:1 stand behind Jesus’ answer to John. 1 Kings 17:17-24 is Elijah raising the widow’s son, the pattern Jesus fulfills. Psalm 103:3 praises the God who forgives all your iniquity. Ephesians 2:8 says we are saved by grace through faith. Hebrews 11:6 says without faith it is impossible to please God. Romans 10:17 says faith comes from hearing. James 1:22 repeats the call to be doers of the word.
application:
Ask yourself: which soil is closest to my heart right now? What would it take to be good soil?

Think of the woman who loved much. What has Jesus forgiven you? Let that fuel your love this week.

Be like the centurion and trust Jesus’ word without needing to see how.
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for his compassion for outsiders and sinners.
Tell him how much you have been forgiven, and let love rise.
Ask him to help you love as one who has been forgiven much.
